subject: Automotive & EVs
title: F1's Hybrid Power Units
description: Learn F1's Hybrid Power Units in one minute.

hook.text: Since 2014, every F1 car runs a turbocharged V6 hybrid—not the screaming V8s fans once loved.

buildup.text: The power unit recovers energy from braking and exhaust heat, feeding it back as electric boost.

discovery.text: These hybrids produce over 1,000 horsepower while using 30 percent less fuel than the old engines.

twist.text: Fans hated the quieter sound, but the technology pushed F1 closer to road-car relevance than ever.

climax.text: Mercedes dominated the first hybrid era, winning eight straight constructors' championships.

punchline.text: The fastest engines are now the most fuel-efficient ones.

quiz.question: What type of engine has F1 used since 2014?

details.summary: Since 2014, Formula One cars use 1.6-liter turbocharged V6 engines paired with two electric energy recovery systems, producing over 1,000 horsepower while achieving thermal efficiency above 50 percent.
details.whyItMatters: F1's hybrid power units are the most thermally efficient internal combustion engines ever built, pushing technology that is feeding directly into road car engine development.
takeaways: The turbo V6 is paired with MGU-K and MGU-H electric recovery systems
Thermal efficiency exceeds 50 percent, double that of a typical road car
Total power output surpasses 1,000 HP from just 1.6 liters

faq.question: What are MGU-K and MGU-H?
faq.answer: MGU-K recovers kinetic energy under braking like regenerative braking in EVs. MGU-H captures waste energy from exhaust gases spinning the turbocharger. Together they convert wasted energy into usable power.

faq.question: Will these engine technologies appear in road cars?
faq.answer: They already are. Mercedes-AMG's One hypercar uses a road-legal version of an F1 power unit. The efficiency insights from F1 inform turbocharged hybrid systems in mainstream Mercedes and other brands.
